Theme

Money, work & business · Work & responsibility

launch verb

bring out something new: a product, a book, a show

also launch a product, launch a book, bring out, put on the market, release, launch a campaign, publication, publish, come out (of a book), the book is not yet out

classical

Cic. Brut. 19: dē rē pūblicā librōs ēdidistī
Lewis & Short: lūdōs ēdere, to put on games
Traupman 366

ēdō, ēdere, ēdidī, ēditum

verb, third conjugation

bring out, publish; put on (a show)

To give out, put forth (Lewis & Short): of a book, to publish it; of games or a show, to put it on. Not edō, edere, to eat, with a short e. To launch a campaign or a big undertaking is to begin it, incohāre (see begin).

Other words

  • vēnāle prōdūcere — put on the market (a new product)

    verb phrase: prōdūcō, prōdūcere, prōdūxī, prōductum · also used · modern · M-O s.v. market: put on the market, after Egger; Ter. Eun. 1.2.54 (old numbering): ancillam prōdūxit, vēndidit (Lewis & Short)

    Classically prōdūcere is to bring out for sale, of slaves in Terence (Lewis & Short); Egger adds vēnāle, for sale.

  • ēditiō, ēditiōnis f. — publication (the act of publishing); an edition

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Plin. Ep. 1.2.5: ab ēditiōne nōn abhorrēre, not to be against publishing; Quint. 5.11.40 (Lewis & Short): an edition

    Post-Augustan (Seneca, Quintilian, Pliny’s letters). The published work itself is liber or opus; to publish is ēdere.

Examples

  • nam ut illōs dē rē pūblicā librōs ēdidistī, nihil ā tē sānē posteā accēpimus

    for since you brought out those books on the State, we have had nothing at all from youCic. Brut. 19

  • Liber ē prēlō nōndum exiit.

    The book is not yet out.Traupman 355

See also begin, advertise, goods, sell.

SourcesLewis & Short: edo · Lewis & Short: produco

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. market.
